statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail sits in the low band while Stress stays elevated on an energy- and rates-driven backdrop.
recommendation: Tail remains well below the block threshold. The cash Nasdaq-100 closed -1.39% but about 169 points above its session low, NQ futures have recovered roughly 0.6% inside a narrow 222-point overnight band, and both Brent and WTI are about 0.9% lower after Thursday's spike, so retracement is functioning and two of the cross-asset amplifiers are de-aligning. The elevated Stress reading describes a difficult high-volatility environment - Brent above 100, a 10-year near 5.23% and an unresolved AI-revenue repricing - rather than an observed mean-reversion failure. The narrow 13:30Z-15:00Z danger window covers the US cash open and the Michigan preliminary release.
headline: NQ futures extend an orderly overnight recovery as oil and yields ease; Tail low, Stress elevated
body: The cash Nasdaq-100 closed Thursday at 30,725.81, down 434.27 points or 1.39%, in a 30,556.40 to 31,125.13 range - a second consecutive decline that still finished about 169 points above the low and roughly 2% below the 31,361.37 fifty-two-week high. The trigger was a Financial Times report that OpenAI's annualised revenue was about 20 billion dollars below previous estimates, which repriced AI-linked names: the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index fell as much as 4% before trimming losses, Arm Holdings, Intel and Marvell each lost more than 6%, and Micron fell more than 5%. Energy and rates amplified Thursday's move - Brent settled at 104.28, up 4%, and WTI at 91.49, up 3.6%, on Strait of Hormuz disruption, while the 10-year yield reached 5.35% intraday before easing to 5.23% against a 4.77% two-year. Both amplifiers have since partly unwound. Brent now trades near 103.35 and WTI near 90.66, each about 0.9% lower, long-term yields have pulled back from multi-decade highs, and no fresh Hormuz escalation has been reported overnight. Current structure is two-sided rather than pathological: NQ December futures trade at 31,152.00, up 182.50 or 0.59%, inside a narrow 30,953.00 to 31,174.75 overnight band, with S&P futures +0.26%, Dow futures +0.11% and Russell futures +0.33%. VIX closed at 15.41, low for a two-day technology decline. Asia firmed into the weekend, with the Hang Seng up 1.80% to 24,213.66 after Thursday's 1.43% loss, the Nikkei up 0.05% and the Shanghai Composite up 0.16%, while Thursday's European closes were weak at DAX -1.18% and Euro Stoxx 50 -0.87%. No persistent one-way NQ structure, shallow-pullback sequence or failed-retracement pattern has been observed, so Tail is held at 17 while Stress reflects the residual energy, rates and AI-narrative stack. Shared Finviz context was not usable this run: the file carries a 2026-09-29T23:14:22Z collection timestamp and a partial collection status, far outside the 90-minute freshness limit, so the assessment rests entirely on independent research.

lookbackSummary: All 24 preceding clock-hours carry a published Claude assessment. The window opens green with Tail 14 and Stress 55, deteriorates through the European and US morning as the AI-revenue story and the energy move developed - Tail entering the watch band from the 07:00Z hour and peaking at 28 with Stress 72 in the 17:00Z hour, the only orange slot - then improves steadily after the US cash close. The last eleven hours are green with Tail between 16 and 18 and Stress decaying from 65 to 54, consistent with retracement resuming once the cash session ended.
outlookSummary: The horizon splits into a live Friday session and a weekend halt. Through the European morning Tail oscillates between 18 and 19 on liquidity transitions rather than observed structure. It enters the watch band at 20 in the 12:00Z pre-market hour, rises to 22 in the 13:00Z hour containing the US cash open and peaks at 23 in the 14:00Z hour, where the Michigan preliminary sentiment and inflation-expectations release overlaps an unwinding opening auction - the narrow 13:30Z-15:00Z danger window. Escalation beyond the watch band would require actually observed opening-auction continuation with shallow pullbacks, in the Aug 4 pattern; an orderly print with visible retracement instead argues for a quick step down, and the 17:00Z and 18:00Z hours are published back in the low band on that basis. A secondary rise to 21-22 covers the power hour into the 20:00Z cash close, where Friday weekend-risk reduction and the scheduled Fed Collins speech meet a thinning book. From 21:00Z the CME weekend halt removes any tradable price path, so Tail collapses to a 10-12 floor and Confidence steps down toward 67 to reflect the absence of live price-path evidence; the unresolved Hormuz blockade and AI-revenue narrative convert into Sunday reopen-gap exposure rather than intraday path risk.
